title: One suite of T-495's claimable half: strategy-to-moves-contract rewritten from a source-text scanner into a behavioural suite, and wired
scope: One suite, because T-495's acceptance is per suite. The other 13 rows of its draw are untouched and keep their T-492 verdicts.
The gated half of T-495 -- the three rows carrying textIsTheSubject -- is NOT touched here. It needs a lane decision from the owner.
This record exists so the T-770 control resolves this path's classification from the LATEST record rather than from the T-492 draw, which is left as the historical draw it is.
method: Re-verified on origin/main 9527130353 by running the suite, not by reading it: 1 failed of 11, and the failure was the byte assertion the item names.
The scanner case was DELETED rather than repaired, per the acceptance. A tighter pattern would have been the same defect with a longer fuse.

Replacement cases drive the real synthesizeStream. Only the audited Anthropic client is mocked, because it is I/O; the classifier, the registry builders and the deterministic fallback all run for real.
Expected strings are produced by calling the registry's own builders, so no literal in the suite can drift from the registry.
Five mutations against the product, each verified to have changed the file before the suite was run.

suites.toContainNote: 42 toContain calls remain and none reads a repository file. Every one asserts over a string a product function returned -- the synthesizer's emitted answer, the captured model input, or the registry's own output. The count is recorded because a scanner detector that counts toContain would flag it, and the distinction that matters is the subject, not the matcher.
suites.rationale: The deleted case asserted 24 substrings of four source files. It was red because synthesizer.ts no longer contains the literal 'const finalText = applyCxoAnswerModeFallbacks(cleanedText, answerMode)' -- the call is still made, at synthesizer.ts:825, written as a ternary arm. It would also have passed with the feature unwired so long as the words stayed. Three behavioural cases replace it: the classified mode's system contract and prompt directive must reach the model, read through the synthesizer's own onModelInput hook; the mode's deterministic fallback must reach the caller, asserted as equality against applyCxoAnswerModeFallbacks over the model's text; and a general-mode query must receive no mode contract at all, which is the case that fails when the injection is made unconditional.

mutations.catches: the deterministic fallback reaching the caller

mutations.note: SURVIVED ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT and the suite was at fault, not the mutation. The general-mode case looped over the four non-general modes only, and `general` declares a systemContract and a promptDirective of its own, so an unconditional injection injected general's contract and no case looked for it. The loop now walks Object.keys(CXO_ANSWER_MODE_REGISTRY), so it covers every mode the registry declares, including modes added later.

mutations.catches: the prompt directive reaching the user message
the system contract reaching the system prompt

residualsNotClosedHere: The deleted case also asserted that src/lib/intelligence/ask/index.ts and src/app/api/intelligence/ask/route.ts contain applyCxoAnswerModeFallbacks( and classifyAbarvaAnswerMode(...). Those were byte assertions over two other modules: they proved the words were present and would have survived the feature being unwired, so deleting them removes a false assurance rather than real coverage. Neither is replaced here, because driving either module means standing up retrieval or a Next.js route, which is a larger unit than this suite. Recorded as a note on T-495.

The directory src/lib/intelligence/ask/__tests__ still cannot be wired whole. Measured on this base: 2 failed suites of 23, and the second is ask-guardrails.test.ts, which T-497 left red on purpose behind an owner decision. The item's own note calls this suite the single blocker on that directory; that is wrong, and the correction is recorded on the item.

OBSERVED, NOT FIXED. buildCxoAnswerModeSystemAddendum and buildCxoAnswerModePromptDirective have exactly one caller between them -- synthesizer.ts -- and it is guarded by answerMode !== "general". CXO_ANSWER_MODE_REGISTRY.general declares both a systemContract (GENERAL_ADVISORY_CONTRACT) and a promptDirective, so neither can reach a model through this path. Whether that is deliberate (the role prompt may already carry the same posture) or a gap is a question about what is sent to the model on every general-mode answer, so it is not changed here and not asserted either way. Checked and NOT a finding: the registry holds 11 entries against 5 in AbarvaAnswerMode, but all six extra entries are active:false and declare no systemContract and no promptDirective, so the narrower type is correct and no authored contract is stranded by it.
